The test image shows a corn **stem/stalk** with large, irregular tan/white bleached lesions with brown borders on the lower stalk, and some smaller dark spots higher up. Plant part is stem.

Stem candidates from index: Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback, Bacterial_Stalk_Rot, Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Common_Smut, Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Head_Smut, Physoderma_Brown_Spot, Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Purple_Leaf_Sheath, Stewart_S_Disease.

Top candidates based on visual: Bacterial_Stalk_Rot (water-soaked tan), Stewart_S_Disease (bleached), Physoderma_Brown_Spot (dark spots on stalk), Purple_Leaf_Sheath (dark lesions on stalk). Viewing one reference from each.

Bacterial_Stalk_Rot shows general rot/collapse, not matching well. Stewart's Disease shows bleached streaks on leaves, more linear. The test image has large irregular tan patches with brown borders on the stalk. Checking Physoderma_Brown_Spot stem and Anthracnose stem next.

Physoderma_Brown_Spot shows dark purple/black spots — doesn't match the pale bleached patches in the test image. Anthracnose stem shows internal brown rot with shiny black external areas — also doesn't match.

**Summary of analysis:**
- Test image: lower stalk/leaf sheath with large, irregular pale tan/white bleached patches with brown/dark borders; plant still green and standing; small dark spots visible higher on stalk
- Bacterial_Stalk_Rot reference: general brown collapse/rot — no discrete bordered patches
- Stewart's Disease reference: more linear bleached streaks along the leaf
- Physoderma_Brown_Spot reference: dark purple/black spots, opposite coloring
- Anthracnose reference: internal stalk rot with shiny black external areas

The large, irregular, pale/bleached lesions with wavy brown borders on the lower stalk/sheath most closely resemble **Goss's Wilt** (large water-soaked gray-green to tan lesions with wavy edges), even though the part index classifies it under leaf/whole_plant. Among the stem-indexed candidates, **Stewart's Disease** (bleached stalk/sheath patches, also in stem category) is the next best fit given the bleached irregular areas visible.

Given the irregular pale bleached patches with distinct brown borders, and that Stewart's Disease explicitly appears in the stem category and produces bleached patches on stalk tissue, I'll assign Stewart_S_Disease as the prediction.
